title: No Montanist prophet was persecuted or martyred
english: So when they called us prophet-killers because we did not receive their prophets who speak without measure—for they say these are the ones the Lord promised to send to the people—let them answer us before God: is there any one of these, my excellent friends, who began to speak from Montanus and the women, who was persecuted by Jews or killed by lawless men? No one. Was any of them seized and crucified for the name? No indeed. Was any of the women ever scourged in the synagogues of the Jews or stoned? Nowhere, in no way. Montanus and Maximilla are said to have died by a different death. For when a spirit that harms the mind stirred each of them, the report is widespread that they hanged themselves—not together, but each at the time of his or her own death. And so they died and ended their lives after the manner of Judas the traitor. Likewise, a widespread report holds that their so-called wonderful Theodotus, the first steward, so to speak, of their so-called prophecy, once when he was being lifted up and taken up into the heavens, fell into ecstasy and entrusted himself to the spirit of deceit, and having been hurled down, died miserably. But do not think, blessed one, that we know such things without having seen them. For perhaps Montanus and Theodotus and the woman mentioned above died in this way, and perhaps not.
orientation: The author is answering the Montanist charge that the church rejected the prophets whom the Lord promised to send, by asking whether any of the Montanist prophets suffered persecution or martyrdom.

title: Testing the spirit that spoke through Maximilla
english: And let not the spirit speaking through Maximilla say, in that same work against Asterius Urbanus, “I am persecuted like a wolf from the sheep; I am not a wolf. I am word and spirit and power.” But let it clearly show the power in the spirit and let it be refuted. And let it compel those who were present then to confess through the spirit, so that men of repute and bishops, Zoticus from the village of Comana and Julian from Apamea, might test and speak with the spirit speaking. But the followers of Themison silenced their mouths and did not allow the false and people-deceiving spirit to be refuted by them.

Then again, after saying other things in between to refute the false prophecies of Maximilla, he at the same time indicates the time when he wrote these things and recalls her predictions, through which she foretold that there would be wars and upheavals. And he corrects their falsehood, speaking as follows:

And how has this lie not already become obvious? For it is more than thirteen years to this day since the woman died, and no war, either partial or universal, has come upon the world. On the contrary, there has been lasting peace for Christians, by the mercy of God.
orientation: The author is refuting the Montanist claim by quoting Maximilla's own saying and then showing that the spirit speaking through her refused to be tested by bishops.
